clue.text: Fall back in marathon, mutually

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Two runners in a marathon fall back together, keeping pace with each other.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's hidden-word step had no indicator; 'in' is it. 'back' then reads NMUTUA the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: Fall is the American name for the season between summer and winter.

clue.text: Clever to take in mineral and cordial

indicators.note: to take in says the word for clever holds the mineral

parts.note: able means clever
mica is a flaky silicate mineral

explanation.surface: A clever drinker mixes a mineral water with a fruit cordial.
explanation.walkthrough: Cordial looks like a drink beside 'mineral'; it is the adjective meaning friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean friendly and warm in manner.

clue.text: Paddy, worker having drink after time

indicators.note: after puts the worker and drink following the time piece

parts.note: an ant is the classic worker insect
rum is a drink

explanation.surface: A worker who has a drink after closing time.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddy is British slang for a fit of temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are outbursts of bad temper, as in 'in a paddy'.

clue.text: Start of route shown in diagrams prepared for carnival

indicators.note: shown in says that letter appears inside the rearranged word
prepared means made ready, so the letters of diagrams are reworked
start of says only the first letter of route is taken

explanation.surface: The parade route is drawn up in diagrams ready for the carnival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges DIAGRAMS into MADIGRAS, and 'shown in' sets the R from 'Start of route' inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mardi Gras is the Shrove Tuesday festival celebrated with carnival parades.

clue.text: With the Italian during tense period towards the end of the day?

definitions.text: period towards the end of the day?

indicators.note: during says the first pieces come inside the word for tense

parts.note: tense means tight, as a stretched rope is
il is the Italian word for the

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson: combining 'with' and an Italian article in some tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusk, the dim light after sunset, comes as the day ends; the question mark admits the description is loose.

clue.text: Look at what I'm doing with room: more information later

parts.note: 'watch this' is what someone says when showing off
space means room

explanation.surface: Someone shows off what they're doing with a room, promising details later.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase tells an audience that further news is on its way soon.

clue.text: Revolutionary leader left — number's up?

indicators.note: in a down clue up says the number is read from bottom to top

parts.note: nine is a number

explanation.surface: A revolutionary leader has fled; is his number up?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests something turned round, but it is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: He led the Bolshevik revolution in Russia in 1917.

clue.text: Unwanted stuff bishop kept in lock-up

indicators.note: kept in says the bishop is held inside the lock-up

parts.note: a lock-up is a garage rented for storage
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop stores his unwanted belongings in a rented lock-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Garbage is rubbish, things thrown away as worthless.

clue.text: Hear about object, all the rage

indicators.note: about says the word for hear goes round the object

parts.note: to hear a case is to try it in court
an end is an object or aim

explanation.surface: Listen to talk about an object everyone wants.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trendy is fashionable, currently popular.

clue.text: Go on NHS diet now out, or act independently

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Advice: start an NHS diet now, or go it alone.
explanation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's National Health Service.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means following one's own inclinations without regard to others.

clue.text: Private hotel, second in Queen Street

parts.note: an inn is a small hotel

indicators.note: in says the word for second goes inside the Queen and Street pieces

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: Directions to a private hotel, the second one along Queen Street.
explanation.definitionFit: Innermost thoughts are personal and secret, the most private ones.

clue.text: Regular returned to collect right bottle

indicators.note: to collect says the reversed word gathers the next piece inside it
returned says the word is read backwards

parts.note: even means regular, as in an even pace

explanation.surface: A regular customer comes back to the shop to pick up the right bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottle here is the British informal word for courage, not a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal words for courage, as in 'lose your bottle'.

clue.text: Bring before a court American soldier over in Scottish isle

indicators.note: in says the turned letters go inside the island

parts.note: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde

indicators.note: over says the soldier's letters are turned round

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: An American soldier stationed on a Scottish island faces a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: To arraign is to call someone before a court to answer a charge.

clue.text: Abbreviated answer printed in laborious parliamentary report

indicators.note: printed in says the short answer is set inside the next word

parts.note: laborious work is hard

indicators.note: abbreviated says the word is cut short to its usual short form

parts.note: taken as written, then shortened

explanation.surface: A minister's terse reply recorded in a long-winded parliamentary record.
explanation.definitionFit: Hansard is the official verbatim record of debates in the UK Parliament.

clue.text: Primate's in capital, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly says the word is heard, not written

parts.note: Lima is the capital of Peru

explanation.surface: A news item: a primate is loose in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the two words sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemur is a Madagascan member of the primate order.

clue.text: Glass vessel

definitions.meaning: a large glass for sherry or beer
a sailing ship with fore-and-aft rigged masts

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a tall drinking glass and a two-masted sailing ship.

clue.text: Island protected by munitions regulation

indicators.note: protected by says the island sits inside the munitions

parts.note: ordnance is military supplies and weapons

explanation.surface: An island defended by weapons under some military rule.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinance is an authoritative decree or local by-law.

clue.text: Put in order for recording device

indicators.note: in says that word goes inside the social order

parts.note: a caste is a social order or class
to set is to put

explanation.surface: Sorting things out to get a recording device ready.
explanation.definitionFit: A cassette is a sealed tape case used to record and play sound.

clue.text: Add weight when retiring, needing very large trousers

parts.note: plus means add

indicators.note: retiring is going back, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: OS, outsize, marks very large clothing

explanation.surface: Someone who puts on weight in retirement needs enormous trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: Plus twos are baggy knickerbockers worn for golf, shorter than plus fours.
explanation.definitionFit: These are loose breeches gathered below the knee, a garment worn on the legs.

clue.text: Monk describing naughty dance

indicators.note: describing, in its sense of drawing round, says the monk encloses the next word

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk
naughty means bad

explanation.surface: A monk talks about a racy dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The lambada is a fast, sensual Brazilian partner dance.

clue.text: Vladimir's OK with tea in his country cottage?

parts.note: da is Russian for yes, as Vladimir might say
cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: Vladimir is happy to have tea at his place in the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A dacha is a Russian country house or holiday cottage; 'his' points to the Russian.

clue.text: Tom, perhaps, installing hot water in French castle

indicators.note: installing says the cat takes the next letter inside

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
eau is French for water

explanation.surface: Tom puts in hot water at a French castle.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom looks like a name; it is a male cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Château is the French word for a castle or grand country house.

clue.text: Admission made by one catching cold on steamship

indicators.note: in a down clue on puts the first part above the steamship
catching says the word for one holds the next letter

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: A passenger is let aboard a steamship despite having caught a cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Access is the right or means of entry, which is what admission is.

clue.text: Small company representative has to play a part

parts.note: an MP is an elected representative
to act is to play a part

explanation.surface: A small firm's sales rep must put on a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Compact means small and neatly packed, as a compact car is.

clue.text: One of the Titans finally cut down

indicators.note: cut down says the phrase loses its last letter

parts.note: at last means finally

explanation.surface: One of the Titans is at last cut down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' looks like a last-letter signal but is a synonym, AT LAST.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Atlas was the Titan condemned to hold up the sky.

clue.text: They correspond with a line on page tucked into enclosures

indicators.note: tucked into says these letters are slipped inside the next word

parts.note: pens are enclosures for animals

indicators.note: on puts a and line after the page piece

explanation.surface: Letter-writers send a line on a sheet of paper inside their envelopes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pen pals are friends who write letters to each other; correspond means exchange letters.

clue.text: Man, we hear, behind European message

indicators.note: behind puts the heard word after the European piece
we hear says the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a man is a male

explanation.surface: Gossip about a man lurking behind a European message.
explanation.definitionFit: An email is a message sent electronically.

clue.text: Working together, at home, by agreement

parts.note: in means at home
concert means agreement, as in acting in concert

explanation.surface: Colleagues working side by side from home, as agreed.
explanation.definitionFit: To act in concert is to act jointly, cooperating with others.

clue.text: Leo perhaps in second warning about sailor

indicators.note: about says the first pieces go round the sailor

parts.note: a sign can be a warning or omen
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: Someone called Leo gets a quick warning about a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo, the lion, is one of the twelve zodiac signs; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.

clue.text: Study training stratagem

parts.note: PE, physical education, is training
a ruse is a stratagem

explanation.surface: A coach looks into a cunning plan for the team's training.
explanation.definitionFit: To peruse is to read or examine carefully.
